questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere english-speaking, outside Europe but not the US and somewhere sunny which led me to Australia:)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing experience being on exchange! Met so many new friends, travelled and had a lot of fun, didn't spend much time doing school work which gave me so many opportunities.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, although i spent a lot of time in the beginning doing administrative work to get settled.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The advisor at University of Sydney was super helpful and provided all needed information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Univeristy of Sydney offers guaranteed student accommodation, which is super convenient but also expensive compared to the general market. The university sends out an e-mail about the accommodation options, but you have to act extremely fast to get the popular options such as Queen Mary Building, which I didn't get because I was too slow. But I lived at Scape Sydney Central, which turned out to be really good and I had amazing flat mates who are now my close friends.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Scape Sydney Central was a great choice for me

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can try out different units (courses) the first week and then you have to decide after that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Course catalogue online

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bear in mind that many courses don't have on-site written exams, but grades are based on assignments. So if you want more time for travel and less stress, you can be strategic and choose courses without exams:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the academic level is lower than in Denmark. I put in less effort in Australia but got better grades.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was more similar to want we know from high school in Denmark, with open discussions, group work and registration of absence.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECOP6012 Country Risk Analysis 
ECOP6103 Dynamics of Economic Change 
ECOP6108 Economy-Environment Sustainability 
EDUH4052 Learning in Outdoor Education

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: EDUH4052 Learning in Outdoor Education was a course about outdoor life and hiking, we went on a day trip to Royal National Park and a weekend trip to Blue Mountains. Many exchange students take this course and its very easy academically and very social + a great way to meet friend.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many clubs and activities to join on campus

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every kind of club, i joined hiking club and bouldering club

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Gob traveling, surfing and hiking! The university offers a surf camp which many exchange students do

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Blue Mountains is a 2-hour train ride from Sydney, would recommend

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: To be honest I didn't get any local friends, I was friends with exchange students (from all over the world)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Speaking a foreign language was a bit challenging in the beginning especially when I was tired, but it quickly got much better and in the end I didn't even think about it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aussies are very chill and easy-going and I really enjoyed adapting to that lifestyle

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Choose student accommodation even though its more expensive, because its really convenient, you don't get scammed, and you can meet new friends.
2) Take courses with a lower work load, so you don't have to miss out on social things because you need to study
3) Say yes to the opportunities you get. Life feels unreal being on exchange and so many things happen.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
1) Having fun all the time
2) Meeting new friends that are not usually the people I hang out with
3) Getting more comfortable speaking English
